findings.title: Registered bridge can commit a different shell outcome within its organization
findings.trigger: An accepted shell-a socket submits a valid outcome for a known shell-c admission belonging to the same org.
findings.cause: Manager authenticates socket and org, then passes org and raw outcome to store without comparing outcome.shellId against registered shellId.
findings.impact: Wrong shell can permanently finalize another shell run.

proof.method: Actual ShellsManager plus native ShellRunStore imported through tsx from private gw-d, synthetic registry and socket fixtures, private disposable database. Both shells registered normally; target admission inserted into actual store. No production requests.
proof.cleanup: Private database directory deleted in finally; no script persisted (inline heredoc).

findings.fix: Validate and bind normalized outcome.shellId to the registered shell before committing; add same-org cross-shell regression.

findings.title: Legacy invoke drops invocationKey before manager refusal guard
findings.trigger: Legacy shells.invoke supplied with invocationKey and retried while durability disabled.
findings.cause: Handler reconstructs params without invocationKey, making manager hasOwn guard unreachable for wire callers.
findings.impact: Caller key silently ignored; retry may execute again.
findings.qualification: Source-confirmed existing boundary gap left unclosed by train; no runtime reproduction performed.
